data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure than a single large service if and only if the distribution of operator-level causal factors (deployment philosophy, personnel, infrastructure vendor, library dependencies) across the network has strictly lower entropy than the equivalent distribution within the large service.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the large service has lower operator-level causal entropy (e.g., via internal federation of independent sub-teams) than the decentralized network.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decentralized network is built on a single open-source framework whose dominant branch constitutes a single deployment philosophy.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If entropy is measured at the wrong level (e.g., code-level diversity exists but data layer is monoculture).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The total quantity of redundancy is irrelevant if it is monoculture; the large service's 'strictly more total internal redundancy' is rendered fragile by a single shared deployment philosophy. Independence is a distribution over causes, not a count of instances.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
